title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Tea Party on 1969-12-31
lineage: CD -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of the legendary NYE ’69 show with killer Garcia tones and standout moments like Black Peter, The Eleven and a rare Big Boy Pete.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD release is praised as virtually flawless – crisp, balanced and immersive enough to feel like you’re in the room.  Musically the concert shines with high energy, memorable jams (especially The Eleven emerging from Good Lovin’), rare tracks and strong performances from all five members.  A few aficionados note a slight speed/pitch quirk and occasional missing tom mic, but these are far outweighed by the overall brilliance.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive 5‑star reviews (13/15) highlight both superb soundboard quality and an exceptional performance; only one mixed review tempers the rating slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Exceptionally clear mix with vivid ambience; reviewers call it “crisp” and “like a GD release”.  Minor notes: slight speed/pitch drift reported by one reviewer and occasional missing tom mic, but overall the tape is clean and complete.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Two‑set NYE marathon that balances psychedelic jams with semi‑acoustic moments; rare songs (Big Boy Pete, Mason’s) and inventive segues keep the energy high throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead tone is repeatedly called “killer” and “moody”; his solos on China Cat/Sunflower and Alligator are highlighted.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh receives praise for nonstop jamming and for locking into the drum break that launches The Eleven.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir is noted for his honest, sweet vocal delivery on songs like Mama Tried and Dire Wolf.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s “cannon” fills and a missing Tom C. mic are mentioned; overall drumming drives the high‑energy jams.
